destinations.name: Mittenwald
destinations.description: Painted houses, mountain walks, violin-making heritage, and strong rail access near the Karwendel range.

destinations.name: Staffelsee
destinations.description: A quieter lake landscape near Murnau with islands, gentle walking routes, and regional food stops.

destinations.name: Burghausen Castle
destinations.description: A dramatic ridge-top castle complex with fewer international crowds than Bavaria's headline castles.

destinations.name: Bad Hindelang
destinations.description: A mountain community known for conservation-focused tourism, hikes, and accessible Alpine scenery.

destinations.name: Benediktbeuern
destinations.description: A monastery village and moor landscape with culture, easy rail access, and low-pressure nature trails.

destinations.name: Waginger See
destinations.description: A warm Bavarian lake area with cycling, family-run guesthouses, and local food traditions.

destinations.name: Kochel am See
destinations.description: A lake and art destination with access to Franz Marc Museum and mountain viewpoints.

destinations.name: Partnachklamm Shoulder Trails
destinations.description: Routes near the famous gorge that distribute walkers toward less concentrated viewpoints and trails.

destinations.name: Reit im Winkl
destinations.description: A well-preserved Bavarian village near the Austrian border with cross-country skiing, quiet summer hiking, and no mass tourism infrastructure.

destinations.name: Walchensee
destinations.description: One of Bavaria's deepest and windiest lakes, prized by windsurfers and kitesurfers, with no motorised boats and excellent water clarity.

destinations.name: Sylvensteinsee
destinations.description: A turquoise reservoir in the Isar valley popular with kayakers and photographers, with almost no tourist facilities and a true wilderness atmosphere.

destinations.name: Andechs Monastery
destinations.description: A hilltop Benedictine monastery producing beer since 1455, with a pilgrimage church, panoramic terrace, and local food served in the monastery tavern.

destinations.name: Jachenau Valley
destinations.description: A dead-end valley south of Bad Tölz with no through traffic, working farms, and complete absence of tourist infrastructure. Rare Alpine solitude within 60km of Munich.

destinations.name: Osterseen Lakes
destinations.description: A chain of 21 glacial lakes in a protected nature reserve south of Lake Starnberg, open for wild swimming and cycling with no tourist facilities.

destinations.name: Oberammergau
destinations.description: A frescoed village best known for its Passion Play, with local woodcarving workshops, venison restaurants, and easy access to the Ettal monastery.

destinations.name: Auerberg Hill
destinations.description: A prominent hilltop above Schongau with Celtic Iron Age ramparts, a baroque pilgrimage church, and sweeping 360° Alpine panoramas visited by almost no one.

destinations.name: Hoher Peißenberg
destinations.description: Home to the world's oldest mountain meteorological station (1781), with forested trails and unobstructed panoramas from Munich to the Alps at 988m.

destinations.name: Schliersee
destinations.description: A compact lake village with a local beer garden culture, freshwater fish restaurants, and hiking access to the Spitzingsee plateau above.

destinations.name: Isarhorn Wetlands
destinations.description: Pristine braided river wetlands where the Isar crosses the Austrian border, with nesting golden eagles and almost zero visitor infrastructure. Reached by train.

destinations.name: Falkenstein Ruin Pfronten
destinations.description: The ruined hilltop castle where Ludwig II planned his final and most ambitious project. Free access, 360° panorama, 5km from Neuschwanstein but completely uncrowded.

destinations.name: Alpsee Immenstadt
destinations.description: A deep pre-Alpine lake in the Allgäu with public shoreline access, wind sports, and wild swimming, far from the crowds of the better-known Bavarian lakes.

destinations.name: Hausham Nordic Trails
destinations.description: 42km of groomed cross-country ski trails in the Schliersee valley, used almost exclusively by locals and entirely absent from international winter tourism marketing.

destinations.name: Miesbach
destinations.description: A working Bavarian market town with a weekly farmers market, authentic Christmas market, and local craft breweries untouched by Alpine tourism marketing.

destinations.name: Lautersee
destinations.description: A glacial lake above Mittenwald reachable by a 30-minute forest walk, with mirror reflections of the Karwendel peaks and no facilities whatsoever.

destinations.name: Kloster Ettal
destinations.description: A baroque Benedictine monastery producing liqueur and beer since the 14th century, with guided visits and a local shop, consistently overlooked in favour of Neuschwanstein.

destinations.name: Cogne
destinations.description: A Gran Paradiso gateway with strong nature credentials, mountain huts, and local food culture.

destinations.name: Chamois
destinations.description: A car-free Alpine village reached by cableway, ideal for slow travel and low-emission exploration.

destinations.name: Lago Blu
destinations.description: A small reflective lake with mountain views, best paired with less busy trails and local villages.

destinations.name: Fenis Castle
destinations.description: A medieval castle experience that complements village routes and local cultural stops.

destinations.name: Valpelline
destinations.description: A quieter valley with pastoral landscapes, local cheese traditions, and uncrowded trails.

destinations.name: Bard
destinations.description: A compact heritage village and fortress with museums, rail access, and cultural programming.

destinations.name: Rhemes-Notre-Dame
destinations.description: A peaceful Gran Paradiso valley for wildlife, hiking, and nature-based stays away from tourist pressure.

destinations.name: Introd
destinations.description: A village with castles, rural architecture, and links to quieter Gran Paradiso approaches.

destinations.name: Ollomont
destinations.description: The least-visited valley in the Aosta region, with glacial lakes above 2500m, a traditional fontina dairy cooperative, and trails shared only with ibex.

destinations.name: Torgnon
destinations.description: A high-altitude plateau village surrounded by protected wildflower meadows, accessible by cable car and entirely unknown to foreign visitors.

destinations.name: Gressoney-Saint-Jean
destinations.description: A Walser cultural village in the Monte Rosa valleys with a royal castle, traditional cuisine, and hiking access to high-altitude lakes rarely visited by non-locals.

destinations.name: Arvier
destinations.description: A transit village overlooked by visitors heading to La Thuile, with a glacial lake accessible above it and ancient terraced vineyards producing Enfer d'Arvier DOC wine.

destinations.name: Pont d'Aël
destinations.description: A 2000-year-old Roman aqueduct bridge with a walkable internal maintenance gallery, one of the most remarkable Roman engineering works in the Alps and almost completely unknown.

destinations.name: Fontainemore
destinations.description: A Walser village in the lower Lys valley on a historic balcony trail, with ancient beech forests and Monte Rosa views, receiving almost no visitors despite a train station nearby.

destinations.name: Aymavilles
destinations.description: A village with a four-towered medieval castle and access to two exceptional hidden sites — the Pont d'Aël Roman aqueduct and the Lago di Chamolé high plateau.

destinations.name: Brusson
destinations.description: A mid-valley village in the Ayas valley with a rare peat bog lake, easy summer hiking, and almost no foreign visitors despite good facilities.

destinations.name: Verrès
destinations.description: A fortified village with a square castle ruin and the most authentic medieval carnival in the Aosta Valley, performed by 400 local residents each February.

destinations.name: La Salle
destinations.description: Starting point for the Ru Courtaud, an 18th-century irrigation canal converted into a 14km balcony walking trail with continuous Mont Blanc views and almost no visitors.

destinations.name: Lillianes
destinations.description: A Walser village in the lower Lys valley hosting the only surviving traditional veillà winter gathering, where locals demonstrate spinning, bread-making, and storytelling in patois.

destinations.name: Chambave
destinations.description: A terraced wine village producing Muscat de Chambave DOC on the steepest slopes in the valley, with a harvest season that receives almost no tourism attention.

destinations.name: Perloz
destinations.description: A village above the lower Lys valley with access to one of the oldest beech forests in the Alps, with trees over 400 years old declared a protected natural monument.

destinations.name: Saint-Martin-de-Corléans
destinations.description: One of Europe's largest megalithic sacred sites with menhirs, cult statues, and burial mounds from 3500 BC, located 1km from Aosta city centre and almost completely overlooked.

destinations.name: Colle del Piccolo San Bernardo
destinations.description: A 2188m alpine pass with Roman road ruins, a medieval hospice, and sweeping cross-border views into France, completely overlooked in favour of the famous Great Saint Bernard Pass.

destinations.name: Châtillon
destinations.description: A transit town that no visitor stops in, with a freely accessible medieval castle ruin on a rocky spur above the valley offering panoramic views and complete solitude.

destinations.name: Sanctuary of Machaby
destinations.description: A 12th-century Romanesque sanctuary on a forested ledge above Arnad with original frescoes intact, accessible via a 40-minute forest path and opened by a resident guardian on request.
